facts.statement: The genus Dickosteus was described by Miles and Westoll in 1963.
Dickosteus fossils date to the Middle Devonian period, specifically from the Late Eifelian to Early Givetian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle Devonian: Late Eifelian to Early Givetian

facts.statement: Fossils of Dickosteus have been found in Orkney and Caithness, Scotland.
facts.quote: Fossils are found in Orkney and Caithness, Scotland.

facts.statement: Dickosteus is one of the few placoderm genera for which complete body fossils are known.
facts.quote: It is one of the few placoderms for which complete bodies are known.

facts.statement: Dickosteus is classified as an extinct genus of coccosteid arthrodire placoderm.
facts.quote: Dickosteus is an extinct genus of coccosteid arthrodire placoderm

facts.statement: Dickosteus belongs to the class Placodermi.
Dickosteus is a member of the family Coccosteidae.
Dickosteus lived during the Givetian stage, approximately 387.95 to 382.31 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Givetian to Givetian (387.95 to 382.31 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Dickosteus was a small placoderm with a total body length of 43.7 cm.
rejected.quote: It was a small placoderm with a total body length of 43.7 cm.
